title: The Borrowed Verdict
premise: Retired detective Edmund Galloway, now tending a failing bookshop, has quietly solved three 'accidental' deaths the police closed years ago. When twin letters arrive — one confessing to all three murders, one promising a fourth — he realizes the killer is someone who knows his secret work and is playing a game with the statute of limitations as a clock. Deciphering a ledger hidden in the shop's inventory reveals the murders were cover-ups of a decades-old police corruption scheme, and the confessor is a dying accomplice seeking absolution while a second, unrepentant conspirator hunts to silence him. Edmund exposes the surviving conspirator publicly just as the statute expires, choosing justice over arrest, but loses the bookshop — and his anonymity — as the price of survival.
about_author: Beatrix Nakamura is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent twenty years transcribing testimony in criminal trials before turning to fiction. She writes quiet, procedural mysteries about ordinary people forced to weigh the law against their consciences.

chapters.title: Marginalia
chapters.summary: Edmund Galloway's POV. In his failing bookshop, Edmund finishes annotating his private file on three 'accidents' he quietly solved. A regular customer, young journalist Priya Raman, notices his marginalia in a donated crime novel. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a man who can no longer stop investigating but no longer has anyone to tell.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Two letters arrive the same morning: one confessing to the three deaths in precise detail only the killer could know, the other promising a fourth and naming Edmund as witness. He verifies the confessor's details against his files. Emotional beat: cold dread — his secret work has been watched, and the game has chosen him.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. A near-fatal 'accident' befalls retired clerk Walter Finch, the fourth letter's predicted victim, who survives and begs Edmund for help. Priya, suspicious of Edmund's calm, starts pulling old case files. Emotional beat: guilt and urgency collide as Edmund realizes the letter was a countdown, not a boast.

chapters.title: Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Following Finch's cryptic hint — 'it was always on your shelves' — Edmund discovers a coded ledger embedded in the prices and accession dates of specific books he acquired at auction years ago. It records payments routed through the three dead men. Emotional beat: revelation and horror — the corruption ran through his own shop.

chapters.title: The Confessor's Voice
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya traces the letters' paper to a hospice and finds the confessor: dying ex-sergeant Arthur Bell, who admits he covered up the scheme to protect his family and now wants the truth out before the statute expires. Emotional beat: pity warring with anger as Bell confesses he used Edmund as his instrument.

chapters.title: Smoke in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The bookshop is torched; the ledger survives because Edmund had begun transcribing it. He recognizes arson as a message from the second conspirator — the man who signed off on the original 'accidents': retired Superintendent Harrow, now a respected civic figure. Emotional beat: rage and resolve; the game turns physical.

chapters.title: What the Statute Keeps
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya and Edmund map the ledger against the statute calendar: Bell's crimes expire in nine days, but Harrow's most recent act — Finch's 'accident' — falls just inside prosecutable limits. Harrow, warned by a leaked tip, begins dismantling evidence and discrediting Finch. Emotional beat: the sickening realization that the law itself may be the killer's final shield.

chapters.title: Bell's Last Chapter
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Bell, fearing Harrow will reach him first, gives Edmund the final ledger key and a sworn recording, then dies that night — officially of natural causes. Edmund knows better. Emotional beat: grief hardening into purpose; the confessor's death converts a puzzle into a debt.

chapters.title: The Borrowed Verdict
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. At a civic ceremony honoring Harrow, Edmund and Priya spring their trap: the ledger, Bell's recording, and Finch's testimony, published simultaneously so Harrow cannot bury it. Harrow attempts to flee and is arrested for the attempt on Finch — inside the statute. Emotional beat: cathartic climax; justice arrives not through the system but through timing, nerve, and truth.

chapters.title: Restocked Shelves
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Weeks later: Harrow awaits trial, Priya's exposé runs, and Edmund — exposed, his quiet life over — reopens the smoke-damaged shop with community help. He shelves Bell's confession in plain sight, uncoded. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; he paid his anonymity and his livelihood for the verdict, and finds it was worth the price.
